'''Luen-Fai Tam''' ([[Traditional Chinese characters|Chinese]]: 譚聯輝, 1947 – 20 November 2025{{citation needed|date=April 2026}}) was a mathematician working in [[differential geometry]], [[general relativity]], and [[complex geometry]]. He was a [[research professor]] at the [[Chinese University of Hong Kong]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.cuhk.edu.hk/people/academic-staff/lftam|title=Prof. Luen Fai TAM &#124; CUHK Mathematics|website=www.math.cuhk.edu.hk|accessdate=Sep 18, 2025}}</ref> 

== Career ==
Tam obtained his PhD in 1984 at [[Stanford University]], advised by [[Robert S. Finn]] with a thesis on the behavior of [[capillary surface]]s in [[low gravity]].<ref name="mg"/> After completing his doctoral studies, Tam was appointed as a research [[assistant professor]] at [[Purdue University]] from 1984 to 1986, where his research shifted towards geometric aspects of [[partial differential equations]]. In 1986, he joined the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] as a [[tenure]]-track assistant professor. From 1987 to 1990, he was a lecturer at the [[Chinese University of Hong Kong]] (CUHK). He then moved to the [[University of California, Irvine]] as an [[associate professor]] in 1990 and was promoted to a [[full professor]] there from 1992 to 1997. Tam returned to CUHK in 1997 as a senior lecturer until his retirement in 2007. Following his retirement, Tam was appointed as a [[research professor]] at CUHK and advised five doctoral students.<ref name="preface">{{cite journal | title=Preface | journal=[[International Journal of Mathematics]] | volume=30 | issue=13 | date=2019 | issn=0129-167X | doi=10.1142/S0129167X19020014 | page=1902001 | url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S0129167X19020014 | ref={{sfnref|International Journal of Mathematics|2019}} | access-date=2025-07-19| url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Tam had published 96 mathematical research articles with over 1,300 citations by 546 mathematicians. His research included [[geometric analysis]], [[harmonic function]]s, [[harmonic map]]s on [[complete manifold|complete]] [[compact manifold|noncompact]] [[Riemannian manifold]]s, [[Mathematics of general relativity|mathematical relativity]], and complex [[Kähler manifold]]s. According to [[MathSciNet]], he had collaborated with 29 mathematicians, including [[Peter Li (mathematician)|Peter Li]] at UC Irvine (Tam's postdoctoral mentor while at Purdue) and [[Yuguang Shi]] at [[Peking University]].<ref name="preface"/>

In honor of Tam's birthday and mathematical contributions, a conference on geometric analysis and mathematical relativity was held at [[Fujian Normal University]] in December 2018.<ref name="preface"/>
